bdx.hubLede: Reputable directories, review platforms, supplier databases, software marketplaces and local-discovery services where a business can create, claim or apply for a public presence.
bdx.indexDesc: A research index of business directories, organised by country and category. Each entry records what a directory accepts, whether listing is free or paid, and how it was verified.

bdx.oppsLede: Find reputable websites where companies, products and professional services can build visibility through public profiles, directories, reviews, marketplaces and supplier listings. Every row is a researched platform; nothing here is a ranking.
bdx.otherCountriesNote: {n} platforms are based in {c} countries that do not yet have a page of their own here. Select one to filter the working list above to it. A country gets its own page once it has enough researched platforms to make one worth reading.
bdx.qualityFallback: Quality is the Directory Score where there is enough evidence to compute one, and a discounted fallback from reputation and status where there is not.
bdx.rankedByScore: Ranked by PetroHrys Score, a first-party editorial assessment of how useful, trustworthy and relevant a directory is for businesses. It is not a Domain Rating, an SEO or authority metric, or a review rating.
bdx.recScoreNote: A Recommendation Score is fit multiplied by platform quality, so a strong platform for a different kind of business scores low here on purpose.
bdx.supranationalDesc: These registries are operated above the level of any single state, so they are listed apart from the national grid. A supranational system often provides access to records that national authorities hold and constitute.
bdx.workingListDesc: A larger working list of reputable platforms for employees and business owners to review, prioritise and submit to. Some details are still unverified and a few entries need a browser check before submitting.

dp.adaptorNote: The three collections are read through an adaptor and never merged: each row keeps its source collection, its own quality signal and its own kind of action. A directory citation is not a press mention and a classified listing is not editorial coverage.
dp.byActionIntro: The same opportunities organised by what you would actually be doing, so the plan reads as a sequence rather than one ranking repeated. Each appears in one group only, and a group that does not apply to this business simply does not appear.
dp.confidenceNote: Confidence is about acting safely, not about prestige. High means the action, route, cost, moderation and effort are all established. Every band lists what it is still missing rather than showing a number on its own.
dp.downloadQueue: Download the full work queue as CSV
dp.healthIntro: How much of each database is actually workable today. These are dataset-quality metrics, not business performance: they measure how much we know, not how well anything performed. The number worth improving is Ready, not the platform count.
dp.honestState: That is the honest state of the catalogue, and it is reported rather than smoothed over by lowering what Ready means.
dp.lede: Choose a business, an objective, a market and a budget, and get a plan you can work through today — what to do, where to do it, what it costs and how sure we are.
dp.needsBrowserIntro: These platforms sit behind a bot filter. The server answered, which proves nothing about the product, so they are neither dead nor ready — they need a human with a rendered browser. This is the single largest unlock available to this dataset.
dp.needsResearchIntro: Relevant platforms where something operational is missing. These are deliberately kept out of the Ready queue: an employee should never discover mid-task that the route was assumed. Each row says exactly what is unknown.
dp.noTrackingNote: There is no completed or submitted state here. Tracking who did what belongs in a system with per-company storage; this is a knowledge base. A header-only tracker template is committed for teams that want to keep that state elsewhere.
dp.readyDefinition: Ready means three things are true: we know what action the platform supports, we have a recorded URL that matches that action, and no known restriction prevents it. It does not mean the submission will be accepted, that it is free, or that anything will be published — an editor may still say no.
dp.readyIntro: Everything here has a known action, a recorded route that matches that action, and no known blocker. Open the link in the last column and do the work. Nothing on this list is a guess: if we did not establish the route, the platform is in one of the queues below instead.
dp.unknownNeverReady: Unknown is never promoted to Ready. A platform whose route we never established is in Needs research, and a platform behind a bot filter is in Needs browser — separate, because they need different work from different people. A blocked request proves the server answered and nothing else, so it never means dead.
dp.whatReadyMeans: What Ready means, and what it does not
evidence.blankMeansResearched: A blank cell means the fact was researched and not established — it never means no.
evidence.wafNote: The server answered, which says nothing about the product.
md.caption: Media, PR and publishing opportunities, highest priority first
md.howToRead1: A media outlet existing is not an opportunity. A contact page is not a submission route, an advertising rate card is not a contributor programme, and a newsroom address is not proof that outside articles are accepted. Every row states the opportunity type that was actually established, and where none could be, the row says so rather than guessing.
md.howToRead2: The types are not interchangeable. Self-publish means you press publish. Press release means the platform carries your announcement. Editorial pitch means an editor decides and usually says no. Contributed article means outside experts can write. Sponsored content means you pay. Journalist source means reporters come looking for you. Reading one as another wastes a week.
md.howToRead3: A blank cell means the fact was researched and not established — it never means no. Platforms behind a bot filter are marked "Needs browser check": the server answered, which says nothing about whether the route exists. An action button appears only where a real URL was found.
md.lede: A global research database of media outlets, press release networks, contributor programmes, startup publications, journalist-source platforms and other publishing opportunities for companies, founders and experts.
md.mediaScore1: Media Score rates the opportunity itself, not your business. It is computed from {d} dimensions — {list} — weighted to {w}. It is never stored; it is recomputed from the record every build.
md.mediaScore2: A platform is scored only when at least {min} dimensions and {mw} of the {w} weight are available. Below that it reads "Not yet scored", which is a statement about our research and not about the platform. {scored} of {total} are scored today; the other {unscored} have no established opportunity route yet.
md.mediaScore3: Media Score does not depend on who is asking. Whether a platform suits YOUR business is a different question, answered by the recommendation pages below, which combine this score with category fit, campaign objective and target market.
md.scope1: Included: media outlets with an established publishing, pitching or contribution route; press release distribution networks; journalist-source platforms; startup and product launch platforms; contributor programmes; and paid editorial products where they are labelled as paid.
md.scope2: Excluded: business directories and company registries, and marketplace and classified platforms — both answer different questions and live in their own datasets. Also excluded, deliberately: link farms, private blog networks, guest-post farms, sites that publish arbitrary unrelated content for money, expired domains, sites whose main offer is selling dofollow links, and anonymous release dumps with no readership. This database is meant to stay compatible with sustainable reputation building, which means refusing rows that would inflate the count.
md.scope3: One publication is one record. Language editions, country mirrors sharing one editorial operation, sections, AMP hosts, and a submission form separate from the publication it serves are not separate opportunities.
md.scopeH: What is and is not here

mon.change.SOURCE_OCCURRENCE_REMOVED: No longer published by one system
mon.emptyBaseline: The monitoring baseline has been initialised. Changes will appear here after the next validated refresh alters an opportunity — installing a monitor is not itself a procurement event.
mon.emptyNoChanges: No semantic changes were detected between the last two validated snapshots.
mon.freshness: Compared against the validated snapshot of {date}.
mon.lede: What changed in public procurement between two validated snapshots — new notices, moved deadlines, cancellations and awards — matched to supplier profiles with the reason shown.
mon.limitDelivery: Email and personalised delivery are not enabled. Monitoring is available on this page and as a CSV export.
mon.limitForeign: Foreign supplier eligibility is never claimed here. No source publishes it per notice, and the eligibility recorded against a platform is a fact about the platform, not about any tender it carries.
mon.limitRetention: The change ledger retains the most recent {n} events. It is observability for recent runs, not a historical archive.
mon.methodDeadline: A deadline is only described as extended or shortened when both values resolve to a real instant. Some sources publish a date with no time zone, which spans 26 hours; those changes are shown as “deadline changed” instead.
mon.methodGone: Sources use bounded windows and sometimes fail. A notice absent from the latest snapshot is reported as no longer observed, never as cancelled — and only when the source refreshed successfully with a complete window. Otherwise nothing is reported at all.
mon.methodGoneHeading: Why a disappearance is not a cancellation
mon.methodMatch: Relevance is scored from the classification codes the buyer published, the geography and whether a route to act exists. It is a relevance score, never a probability of winning.
mon.methodNew: It means new to our monitoring, not necessarily newly published. A notice can enter the corpus because a source window moved, while the buyer published it weeks earlier. The publication date is shown on the opportunity itself.
mon.notLive: Monitoring compares validated opportunity snapshots. It is not a real-time feed, and the refresh is run manually.
mon.reason.CHANGE_DEADLINE_CHANGED_UNCOM: the deadline changed but the two values cannot be compared
mon.reason.CHANGE_NO_LONGER_OBSERVED: absent from the latest validated snapshot
mon.reason.CHANGE_STATUS_CHANGED: the source reported a new status
mon.reason.CONFIRMED_BY_TWO_SOURCES: published by more than one system

mon.reason.MATCH_TITLE_TERM: a sector term appears in the official title
mon.reason.SECOND_SOURCE: a second official system carries it
mon.showing: Showing {shown} of {total} alerts. The CSV export carries all of them.
mon.sourcesIntro: Change detection depends on knowing whether a source actually refreshed. A source that is not healthy and complete cannot report an opportunity as having disappeared.
mon.threeLayers: Three layers sit under this page. Tender & Procurement Platforms says where procurement happens. Tender Opportunities says what is open. Monitoring says what changed since the last validated refresh.

mp.caption: Marketplace and classified platforms
mp.lede: Platforms where a business or a person can publish a listing — goods, vehicles, property, jobs or services. This is a different question from a business directory, which is about publishing a company profile, and the two datasets are kept apart.
mp.scope: What is and is not here
mp.scope1: Included: classified portals, local marketplaces, buy and sell sites, and vehicle, property, job and service classifieds. Excluded: business directories and company registries, which answer a different question and live in their own dataset; pure retail shops, price comparison sites, news portals and forums.
mp.scope2: Where one operator runs several national sites — OLX, Adevinta, the Bazos network — each national site is its own row, because each is a separate listing and a separate account. A second domain serving the same country from the same operator is not.
mp.searchPlaceholder: Marketplace, country, type or listing model
mp.summary: {n} platforms across {c} countries. A blank cell means the fact was researched and not established — it never means no. Platforms behind a bot filter are marked "Needs browser check": the server answered, which says nothing about the product.
mp.title: {n} marketplace and classified platforms in {c} countries
rec.lede: {n} ranked places where a {p} business can publish, pitch, submit or sponsor — with the reason for every ranking.
rec.lim1: The ranking is only as good as the underlying facts. Where a platform sits behind a bot filter its route could not be read, and the row says so — treat those as leads to confirm in a browser, not as verified opportunities.
rec.lim2: Media Score carries no traffic, Domain Rating or audience figures, because this repository measures none of those and will not estimate them. It is an editorial reading of the opportunity, not a prediction of results.
rec.method1: This profile is declared abstractly: publication categories ({cat}){adj}, industries ({ind}) and subject keywords. It names no platform. Every result below is produced by matching those declarations against the registry, so the same rules that ranked this page rank every other one.
rec.method2: A recommendation combines four things: how well the publication serves this kind of business, whether its opportunity type delivers the objective, whether it reaches the target market, and the intrinsic Media Score of the opportunity. A platform with no Media Score is still recommended, at a discount, because an unscored platform reflects a gap in our research rather than a fault in the platform.
rec.method3: Explicit negative evidence disqualifies: a platform that has closed, was rejected on quality grounds, or offers no opportunity type capable of delivering the objective is excluded outright rather than ranked low. Missing evidence never excludes.
rec.rankedNote: Ranked by fit for this kind of business, not by fame. A platform appears here because the engine scored it, never because it was placed here by hand.
rec.title: Media opportunities for {p}
tdp.classificationNote: Assigned by the source under CPV or UNSPSC. These are separate vocabularies and are never mapped onto one another.
tdp.descriptionExcerpt: Extract as recorded from the source. Read the official notice for the full text.
tdp.factsNote: Recorded as published. Dates without a stated time zone are shown exactly as written.
tdp.freshness: Based on the latest validated procurement snapshot. This page is not a live feed.
tdp.lede: Procurement opportunity published by {buyer}, recorded from {source}. The facts below are the source's; anything derived is labelled.
tdp.limitDocuments: Whether tender documents can be downloaded is not established for this notice. Any document availability recorded elsewhere is a property of the platform, not of this tender.
tdp.limitEligibility: Whether foreign suppliers may bid is not established for this notice. Platform-level evidence is not a statement about this procurement.
tdp.limitSource: This page records what a source published. It is not the official notice and carries no legal weight; the official notice always governs.
tdp.matchesNote: Derived by matching the published classification codes and title against supplier profiles. This is relevance to a profile — not a probability of winning, and not an assessment of competition.
tdp.noClassification: The source published no classification code for this notice.
tdp.noMatches: No supplier profile matches this opportunity strongly enough to report.
tdp.notAffiliated: PetroHrys is not affiliated with the buyer and does not submit bids. Always verify terms on the official notice.
tdp.oneLanguage: This record is published once, in the source's own language for the procurement facts. The tender search and monitoring pages are available in English, German, Spanish and French.
tdp.passedButOpen: The published deadline has passed while the source still reports this notice as open; both facts are shown as recorded.
tdp.provenanceNote: Every source that published this procurement. One opportunity, however many sources carried it.
tdp.relatedNote: Distinct procurements from the same buyer with very similar wording. They are not duplicates: each has its own deadline, status and notice.
tds.browserCheckNote: This source needs a real browser to verify — that is a property of the source, not a doubt about the tender
tds.deadlineNotComparable: The deadline has no time zone, so it is shown as published and not counted in days
tds.defaultSort: With no query, results are ordered by deadline, soonest first. This is not a ranking of quality or of how likely a bid is to succeed.
tds.emptyHint: Try removing a filter or using fewer words. No substitute results are shown.
tds.f.browserCheck: Source needs a browser to verify
tds.heading: Search open tenders
tds.intro: Search {n} current procurement opportunities from the sources below. Filtering and ranking happen in your browser; nothing you type is sent anywhere.
tds.loadFailed: The search index could not be loaded. The tables further down this page still work, and the CSV carries every opportunity.
tds.methodBrowserCheck: Some sources need a real browser before their pages can be verified. That is a property of the source, and says nothing about whether a tender is genuine or worth bidding for.
tds.methodClassification: Tenders are classified by their source under CPV or UNSPSC. These are separate vocabularies and are not merged or mapped onto one another. The scheme is always shown next to the code, and codes are searchable exactly.
tds.methodCurrency: Declared values are shown in the currency the source published, and are never converted. Ordering by value therefore requires choosing one currency first.
tds.methodDeadline: A deadline is counted in days only when it resolves to an unambiguous moment. A date published without a time zone spans more than a day, so it is shown exactly as published and left out of the closing-within filters rather than being guessed into one.
tds.methodDiversity: When your words also appear in a buyer's name, every notice from that buyer scores identically. Results that tie are ordered to vary the buyer and the wording rather than by an arbitrary internal identifier. Results with different relevance are never reordered, so nothing less relevant is ever promoted.
tds.methodDocuments: Whether tender documents can be downloaded is recorded for the platform as a whole, never for an individual notice, so there is no per-tender documents filter. Adding one would state something no source established.
tds.methodFactVsDerived: Each result separates three things: what the source published, what we derived from it, and how the observation was made. Only the first is a fact from the buyer. A supplier-profile match is our calculation, not a statement by anyone procuring anything.
tds.methodIndexing: Filters and searches change this page's address so a search can be shared or reopened, but those addresses are deliberately kept out of search engines: they are states of one page, not thousands of separate pages.
tds.methodRelated: Some buyers publish many closely worded notices at once. Where wording, buyer, country and classification all agree, those opportunities are shown together under one result so a single procurement programme does not fill the page. Nothing is merged or removed, and every opportunity remains in the result count.
tds.methodRelevance: Relevance to your words and supplier-profile match are two different measurements and are never combined into one score. Choosing a supplier profile narrows which tenders are shown; it does not change how your words are ranked.
tds.methodSearchable: Your words are matched against the tender title, the buyer name, classification codes and their published labels, and a short extract of the description. A title match counts for more than a description match, and an exact classification code counts for most. Put a phrase in quotation marks to require those words together.
tds.methodSourcePlatform: Every source in this collection currently publishes from exactly one procurement platform, so choosing a source and choosing a platform would select the same records. Only one control is offered rather than two that appear to differ.
tds.methodUnknown: Unknown is kept as unknown. A notice that does not mention electronic submission is not recorded as refusing it, and it is reachable through the “Not stated” option rather than being folded into “No”.
tds.noscript: Search needs JavaScript. Without it, the tables further down this page and the CSV still list opportunities.
tds.notice.valueSortNeedsCurrency: Ordering by declared value needs a single currency chosen first. Values are published in 13 different currencies and are never converted, so ordering across them would be meaningless. Results are ordered by deadline instead.
tds.relatedNote: Distinct procurements from the same buyer with very similar wording. They are not duplicates: each has its own deadline, status and notice, and each is counted separately in the result total.
tds.searchPlaceholder: Words, a buyer, or a CPV or UNSPSC code
toi.closingIntro: Only opportunities whose deadline can be resolved to a real instant appear here — {decidable} of {current}. A deadline published without a time zone is shown on its record but never used to decide whether something is still open.

toi.freshness: Latest ingested opportunities. Refreshed manually; last ingestion {date}. This is not a live feed, and nothing here updates between refreshes.
toi.lede: {current} currently open procurement opportunities, ingested from {sources} official sources and matched to supplier profiles using the classification codes the buyers themselves published.
toi.limitCoverage: Each source is ingested over a bounded, documented window rather than in full. Where the window could not be exhausted, the source table says so.
toi.limitDeadline: Some sources publish a deadline with no time zone, and one publishes no deadline at all. Those are shown exactly as published and are never used to assert that something is still open.
toi.limitForeign: Foreign supplier eligibility is never claimed here. No pilot source publishes it per notice, and the eligibility recorded against a platform is a fact about the platform, not about any tender it carries.
toi.limitHistorical: {n} ingested records are historical rather than current — awarded, closed, or withdrawn, including {cancelled} cancelled. They are kept for the record and excluded from every recommendation.
toi.limitNoValue: Contract value appears only where the buyer published one. Nothing is estimated, converted between currencies, or summed across lots.
toi.noClosing: No opportunity in the current corpus has a resolvable deadline inside this window.
toi.noMatches: No currently open opportunity in this corpus matches this profile.
toi.notAWinScore: This is an opportunity match, not a probability of winning. Nothing in the published data supports estimating competition, bidder numbers or chances, and none of those is calculated here.

toi.profileNote.engineering: Matched on architectural, engineering, inspection and research codes.
toi.profileNote.it-software: Matched on software package, information system and IT service codes.
toi.profileNote.logistics: Matched on transport service and auxiliary transport codes.
toi.profileNote.manufacturer: Matched on industrial machinery, electrical equipment, transport equipment and furnishings codes.
toi.profileNote.telecom: Matched on telecommunications network and equipment codes specifically, not on the whole of CPV division 32 or 64 — those also contain photographic film and postal services.
toi.profilesIntro: Each opportunity is scored against a supplier profile on category fit, geography, whether a route to act exists, how much time is left, and how well established the facts are. Only currently open opportunities are ranked.

tp.caption: Tender and procurement platforms with jurisdiction, operator, verified routes and evidence status.
tp.intelligenceLink: Procurement Intelligence: which of these systems to investigate first, by supplier type
tp.lede: A verified database of public and institutional procurement platforms, tender portals and supplier systems — with the discovery, registration and submission route for each where evidence establishes it.
tp.limit1: Some official platforms sit behind bot protection, cookie gates or script-only shells that cannot be verified without a rendered browser. Those records are published with "Needs browser check" and without any route this research could not confirm.
tp.limit2: Coverage is Wave T1: Europe and adjacent jurisdictions, prioritising official national systems and EU-level infrastructure. Regional, municipal, utility and commercial-aggregator systems are researched in later waves. Russia and Belarus are recorded as unresolved pending a sanctions and accessibility assessment.
tp.method1: Every platform was verified against its own live surface: HTTP status, final URL, page title and body size were recorded, and a deep route is published only when it was separately confirmed to differ from the homepage. A 200 response is not treated as proof, and a bot wall or a script-only shell is never treated as a dead platform — those records say "Needs browser check" instead.
tp.method2: Statements with consequences carry the highest evidence bar. That a foreign supplier may participate is claimed only where the operator or a competent authority states it; it is never inferred from a website being reachable, being in English, or belonging to an EU member state.
tp.method3: This database catalogues platforms. It does not republish tender notices, and it records no invented metrics — no traffic estimates, no contract values, no bidder counts, no scores.
tp.monitoringLink: Tender Monitoring: what changed since the last validated refresh
tp.opportunitiesLink: Tender Opportunities: what is actually open right now, matched to supplier profiles
tp.scope1: A procurement platform here is a system where a company can discover tenders or contract notices, register as a supplier, obtain tender documents, or submit a bid. National systems, EU and institutional systems, development banks and genuinely distinct ecosystem components each get one record.
tp.scope2: It is not a grants database, a business directory, a marketplace, a list of procurement authorities, or a list of procurement software vendors. EU funding portals are procurement look-alikes and are deliberately excluded; a regulator that merely supervises a platform is recorded as the operator of that platform, not as a platform itself.
tp.scopeHeading: What this database is — and is not
tp.summary: {n} platforms across {c} jurisdictions. Discovery, supplier registration, documents and bid submission are separate systems in real procurement ecosystems — a link appears here only where that specific route was verified. Unknown means researched and not established; it never means no.
tp.title: {n} tender and procurement platforms in {c} jurisdictions

tpi.browserSummary: {n} platforms still require verification in a rendered browser. That is a research state, not a quality judgement: a system behind bot protection is not a worse procurement system.
tpi.downloadCsv: Download the intelligence layer for all {n} platforms as CSV
tpi.foreignSummary: Foreign supplier eligibility is verified on {v} platforms and unverified on {u}. Unverified means exactly that — it is not a finding that foreign suppliers are excluded.
tpi.how1: Two different questions are scored separately. Utility asks how strong and actionable a procurement source is: can opportunities be found, is there a registration path, can a bid be lodged, and how well established are those facts. Fit asks how relevant that source is to a particular supplier and objective. A national platform with modest evidence can be the single most relevant source for a supplier targeting that country, and a superbly documented development bank can be irrelevant to a local firm.
tpi.how2: Every value here is derived at build time from the platform records. Nothing is stored, nothing is estimated, and no platform is promoted by hand. Where a fact was never established, the answer is unknown rather than a guess.
tpi.how3: The database records no industry classification. Recommendations for software, telecom, manufacturing or construction suppliers rank general-purpose systems by the capabilities those suppliers need — they do not claim any platform specialises in a sector.
tpi.landscapeIntro: Derived operating models across the whole collection. A homepage is not a route: a platform appears as discovery-only when a search surface was verified and nothing further was.
tpi.lede: Which procurement systems to investigate first, given what kind of supplier you are and what you are trying to do — with the evidence level and the reason shown for every recommendation.
tpi.limit1: Scores measure documented procurement utility, not popularity, contract volume or likelihood of winning. None of those is recorded and none is estimated.
tpi.limit2: Industry recommendations are an editorial mapping from supplier type to the capabilities that matter, applied over recorded facts. They are labelled as editorial wherever they appear.
tpi.limit3: {n} platforms are not yet scored because their own evidence is not established. Scoring them would present a research gap as a measurement.
tpi.rationale.b2b-saas: As IT/software, but weighted further toward electronic submission and catalogue style instruments, since subscription software is rarely procured on paper.
tpi.rationale.construction: Weighted toward established document routes — drawings and bills of quantities live there — and toward national and regional systems, where public works are tendered.
tpi.rationale.energy: Weighted toward utility and institutional buyers and toward established document routes, given the technical specification volume in energy tendering.
tpi.rationale.engineering: Weighted toward consulting instruments — expressions of interest and RFPs — which is how engineering services are commonly procured.
tpi.rationale.eu-company: Combines EU-level and EU national systems with multilateral systems an EU supplier can reach. Geography is relevance, not eligibility: an EU platform does not confer verified eligibility, and the two are scored separately.
tpi.rationale.exporter: Weighted toward verified foreign eligibility and supranational reach — the two facts that determine whether an exporter can participate at all.
tpi.rationale.foreign-supplier: Ranks on verified foreign eligibility first, then on whether a supplier can actually register and submit from abroad. Platforms whose eligibility is unverified are shown, clearly marked, and never presented as foreign-friendly.
tpi.rationale.healthcare: Weighted toward goods instruments and toward institutional and multilateral buyers, which run large medical supply programmes.
tpi.rationale.industrial-supplier: As manufacturer, with more weight on registration, since industrial supply often runs through qualified-supplier registers.
tpi.rationale.infrastructure: As construction, with weight on project-financed surfaces, since large infrastructure is frequently funded by development banks.
tpi.rationale.it-software: Software is usually bought through framework agreements and dynamic purchasing systems rather than one-off works tenders, so systems recording those instruments rank higher. This is an instrument fact from the dataset, not a claim that the platform specialises in IT.
tpi.rationale.local-sme: Weighted toward national, regional and municipal systems with free search and a clear registration path. Multilateral systems rank low here by design, not by defect.
tpi.rationale.logistics: Weighted toward framework agreements and cross-border reach, since transport is usually contracted as a standing arrangement across jurisdictions.
tpi.rationale.manufacturer: Weighted toward goods instruments, cross-border reach and verified foreign eligibility, because manufacturing supply is frequently cross-border.
tpi.rationale.professional-services: Weighted toward consulting instruments and toward institutional and multilateral buyers, which procure advisory work heavily.
tpi.rationale.telecom: Weighted toward framework agreements and toward institutional and utility buyers, which is where communications services are typically contracted. The dataset does not record sector specialisation and none is claimed.
tpi.reason.certainty: rests on operator or directly observed evidence
tpi.reason.consultingInstruments: expressions of interest or RFPs are recorded
tpi.reason.discovery: a tender search route is established
tpi.reason.foreignVerified: foreign eligibility is verified by the operator
tpi.reason.frameworkInstruments: framework agreements or dynamic purchasing systems are recorded
tpi.reason.localReach: covers national, regional or municipal procurement
tpi.reason.registration: a supplier registration route is established
tpi.reason.submission: a bid submission route is established
tpi.recIntro: Ranked from {n} publishable platforms. Fit orders each list; utility breaks ties.
tpi.title: Procurement Intelligence: {n} platforms scored across {p} supplier profiles
